back: A statement about what is, was or will be, which can be tested against evidence and shown to be true or false.
A statement involving a value judgement about what ought to be; it cannot be settled by evidence alone.
Other things being equal: all other influences are held constant to isolate one relationship.
A simplified representation of reality built on assumptions and used to explain and predict.
Different value judgements; different models, assumptions or data; different time horizons.
The period in which at least one factor of production is fixed.
The period in which all factors of production can be varied but technology is unchanged.
The period in which all factors can be varied and technology can change.

front: Does a positive statement have to be true?
back: No. It only has to be testable; evidence may show it is false.
